speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the nature of the feeding difficulties and when the abdominal distension began?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the baby have a fever, and have you noticed any vomiting or changes in stool color, such as it being bloody or pale? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the baby passed any stool recently, and if so, was it meconium or normal breastfed/formula stool? Also, did the baby pass meconium within the first 48 hours of life?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the baby pass meconium within the first 48 hours of life, and has he passed any stool since then? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray findings of dilated bowel segments with an empty rectum are highly suggestive of Hirschsprung disease. I will request a rectal suction biopsy to confirm the absence of ganglion cells. REQUEST TEST: Rectal_Suction_Biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the biopsy is normal, we must consider other causes like meconium ileus or small left colon syndrome, especially given the distension and feeding issues. Does the family have a history of cystic fibrosis, and has the baby had any episodes of respiratory distress or failure to thrive since birth? REQUEST TEST: Sweat_Cl_Test

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal sweat test and biopsy, I need to rule out other obstructive causes. Has the baby passed any stool since birth, and if so, was it delayed? REQUEST TEST: Contrast_Enema

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: A transition zone in the distal colon, compatible with Hirschsprung disease

speaker: Doctor
text: The contrast enema shows a transition zone, which is classic for Hirschsprung disease despite the initial normal biopsy. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung disease
